title: Ukraine brings down a road span of the Kerch Bridge between Russia and Crimea
seoTitle: Kerch Bridge strike: road span collapses into the strait
dek: After drone and missile strikes on 16 and 17 November, one arch and the road span beneath it fell into the Kerch Strait, leaving a gap in the roadway. Russia reports no casualties; rail traffic resumed on one track.
happened: Ukrainian drones hit the road navigation span of the bridge linking Crimea with Russia's Taman Peninsula overnight from 15 to 16 November, during one of Ukraine's largest drone attacks, and a second wave late on 16 November brought the span down. Reuters-verified imagery cited by Military.com shows one metal arch and the road span beneath it collapsed into the strait, leaving a gap in the roadway; Maritime Executive reports the rubble fell into the strait's only navigation channel. Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) says the operation ran for about a month in seven stages, first targeting Russian air defences. President Zelensky says "Palianytsia" drones hit the road section and "Neptune" missiles and other drones the rail section. The parallel rail bridge is still standing; Ukraine's General Staff says its arch "has already been damaged". Russia's Transport Ministry reported no casualties. Vladimir Putin led the first convoy across the bridge when it opened in 2018; it is a key freight route for Russian forces.

sides.says: The SBU says one arch and the road span were "completely destroyed". Zelensky wrote: "We are reminding Russia that war will always return to where it began." Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara said: "The strike was carried out exclusively with Ukrainian weapons." The General Staff says the road section "is out of service".

Russia's Investigative Committee called it a "terrorist act by Ukrainian armed groups". Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said a repair plan would make the bridge "even better than before"; Maritime Executive reports an earlier Kremlin description of the damage as "minor". The Transport Ministry says "experts are assessing the damage". Sergei Aksyonov, the Russian-installed head of Crimea, said passengers without vehicles could use a ferry.

The bridge spans the channel used by ships entering and leaving the Sea of Azov. Andrey Sizov of Sovecon told Reuters the collapse could "substantially delay" a return to shipping because debris must be cleared. No formal closure of the channel has been reported.

next: Rail traffic resumed on one track on 17 November while repairs continue on the other, according to Russia's Transport Ministry as reported by Vedomosti. The strike came two days before Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping were due to meet in Shenzhen, China, on 19 November.
summary: Ukrainian drone and missile strikes on 16 and 17 November brought down one arch and a road span of the Kerch Bridge, the link between Russia and occupied Crimea, leaving a gap in the roadway and debris in the shipping channel to the Sea of Azov. Ukraine says the road section is out of service; Russia calls it a terrorist act, reports no casualties and says it will repair the bridge. Rail traffic resumed on one track.

conflicts: Day of the strike: Maritime Executive describes hits overnight on 15-16 November and a second wave on the night of 16 November that destroyed the span; Military.com reports the attack on Tuesday, 17 November.
Damage: the Kremlin first called it "minor" (Maritime Executive); Ukraine's SBU says the arch and road span were "completely destroyed", and imagery cited by Military.com shows the span in the water.
